influences.name: Nina Simone
influences.context: As a child Gabriel listened to church music, hymns, classical and most of all soul. He was drawn to the soul singers in terms of what they could do with their voice and storytelling. As an example, he mentions how Nina Simone sang the protest song 'Strange Fruit' about the lynching of African Americans.

influences.name: The Beatles
influences.context: he mentions how Gabriel says he can remember the exact moment as to where he was when he first heard certain songs such as 'Love Me Do' by the Beatles; in the back of his parents' car.

influences.name: Daniel Lanois
influences.context: This would drive Daniel Lanois, the co-producer of the 'So' album nuts. In the documentary series 'Classical albums' Lanois talks about the extremes measures he took to in order to make Gabriel finish the songs.

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: The Beatles, the Stones, the Who, definitely... both the Beatles and the Stones, just to name a couple, have him creamed there

influences.name: The Who
influences.context: The Beatles, the Stones, the Who, definitely.

influences.name: The Doors
influences.context: The Doors, sure - after all, they did manage to successfully merge roots-rock with a style that had nothing to do with roots-rock.

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: essentially the closest Gabriel ever came to sounding like Bob Dylan

influences.name: Robert Fripp
influences.context: killer guitar solo from Robert Fripp (who also produced the album)

influences.name: Tony Levin
influences.context: the only majorly notable person to regularly work with Peter is one Tony Levin, one of the finest session bassists

influences.name: Phil Collins
influences.context: based around Phil Collins' drum pattern

influences.name: David Byrne
influences.context: nearly everything Gabriel has been doing from now on seems to be a WAY worse copy of what David Byrne does

influences.name: Mike Oldfield
influences.context: Mike Oldfield already demonstrated it in Ommadawn, but making those pounding drums sit comfortably next to bagpipes, tin whistles, folk guitar, electric guitar and synthesizers

influences.name: Kate Bush
influences.context: Bush dedicates his life to digging deep into music from outside the US and Europe... Bush even learnt a lot from Gabriel

influences.name: Brian Eno
influences.context: this album was a product of the experimentation on Eno and Byrne's My Life in the Bush of Ghosts

influences.name: Anne Sexton
influences.context: Peter Gabriel has a fascination with Anne Sexton's prose and poetry, evident in 'Mercy Street'

influences.name: Bruce Springsteen
influences.context: Gabriel saw a Springsteen concert around the time he left Genesis, and was very impressed by it; and I can hear traces of 'Born to Run' era Springsteen in the bombastic production of this album

influences.name: The Kinks
influences.context: i wanted the 7" Lola from the Kinks when it became No 1 hit in Swiss Hitparade

influences.name: Tangerine Dream
influences.context: Parallel to such Rock i listended to all them German Synthy guys: Tangerine Dream, Schulze, Peter Baumann etc

influences.name: Kraftwerk
influences.context: my parallel mix of 12" Das Modell from Kraftwerk, German and English version slightly syncopated

influences.name: Pink Floyd
influences.context: Can't imagine a live without Floyd. But i like we are opposits on your blog. Thats fun. I love Pink Floyds ways more than PG, actually, it's my most influencial group i grew up with

influences.name: Yes
influences.context: Yes play much more complex melodies

influences.name: Richie Havens
influences.context: Richie Havens (the one who did the original 'No Opportunity Necessary No Experience Required,' which Yes completely remade on their second album)

influences.name: Steve Howe
influences.context: Peter is not able to write complex melodies like Steve Howe do

influences.name: Simple Minds
influences.context: 'Red Rain' opens with some resplendent Copeland hi-hat work, and ends with the kind of piano/vocal coda that Simple Minds excelled at – the influences were now flowing both ways.

influences.name: Randy Newman
influences.context: 'Big Time' is Gabriel's amusing, self-mocking, Randy Newmanesque satire on success and celebrity

influences.name: George Martin
influences.context: I remember talking to George Martin (Beatles producer) about this as a sort of production technique and he was appalled, because of the waste involved.

influences.name: Peter Green
influences.context: Peter Green is enormously talented and is someone who I think was one of the key British musicians when I was growing up.

influences.name: Robert Lepage
influences.context: I still really enjoy visual things and I think Robert Lepage, who I worked with on the last tour, is a real visionary.

influences.name: Soul and blues artists (general influence period)
influences.context: As a teenager I was very influenced by soul and blues and that was my starting point to a lot of music and I think that this was definitely an influence on that track.

influences.name: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan
influences.context: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan was one of the most extraordinary singers, I think, of our time.

influences.name: Will Gregory
influences.context: I spend a week working with Will Gregory who has been doing the Goldfrapp material with Alison.
